newsitem.title: USA: Maine might get up to $35 mln surplus - treasurer.
newsitem.headline: Maine might get up to $35 mln surplus - treasurer.

text.p: Maine could end the fiscal 1997 year with an up to $35 million surplus, the state treasurer said on Tuesday.
The state plans to use for a short-term stabilization fund as well as tax relief.
"We think it'll be between $25 (million) and $35 million," said Dale McCormick, in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
She added: "And that will be used for the Rainy Day Fund, some will be carried over, some will go into a new tax relief fund."

The legislature has repealed an unfunded cap on income tax receipts that rating agencies had criticized, McCormick noted. Parts of the interview with the state treasurer are scheduled to be aired on Thursday at 1515 EDT.

The Rainy Day Fund, which totals about $38.2 million--two percent of total spending, according to Standard and Poor's Corp--should rise to $45 million, the state controller projected. This was a big leap from the $756,000 level seen in fiscal 1992.
Maine starts its new fiscal year on July 1, and revenues have been higher than anticipated in a number of areas, a report by A.G. Edwards & Sons Inc said.

For the first seven months of the fiscal 1997 year, corporate income taxes produced $12.4 million more than expected, with individual income taxes running $17 million above predictions. Estate taxes climbed $3.68 million over budget, lottery transfers $2.9 million, and investment income $1.9 million, it added.
The state also is setting up reserves for various tax revenues to protect it in case there is an unexpected dip, McCormick said.
Further, due to improved accounting practices, the state has been able to lower net tax receivables to roughly $30 million or so by January 1997 from just over $100 million in January 1995.
